title: Casper and the Signal
premise: Sable Eastwick, a xenolinguist whose mind has drifted so far from human speech that he no longer dreams in it, intercepts a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct for two centuries and spoken by no living soul. The signal comes from a derelict station caught between two hostile fleets on the edge of a fragile truce, and its message is a lie Sable must keep alive: a fabricated plea for peace that only he can sustain in a dead tongue. As the truce clock runs down, Sable assembles a ragtag crew of castoffs who become the family he never had, each of them hiding inside their own invented self. In the end, Sable chooses to broadcast the truth instead of the lie, gambling that two fleets tired of war will accept an honest silence over a beautiful falsehood — and the station's survivors, speaking Vessic through him, find a home among his crew.
about_author: Wendell Pemberton is the pen name of a former shipping-route radio operator who spent eleven years listening to languages he never learned to speak. He writes from a decommissioned relay buoy off the coast of Maine, where he claims the static still talks back.

chapters.title: The Tongue That Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Aboard the long-haul freighter Meridian, Sable finishes another silent route between colonies that have stopped answering, haunted by dreams in languages that aren't human anymore. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic — extinct, impossible, addressed with his old certification code — he answers against protocol. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by a voice that finally speaks his frequency.

chapters.title: A Lie Held by Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, widening to the crew he gathers: disgraced medic Iyo, ex-fleet gunner Brask, and stowaway engineer Tamsin. They reach the derelict station Halcyon Reach and discover the signal is a fabrication left by dying Vessic loyalists — but both approaching fleets believe it, and the truce holds only while the fiction does. Emotional beat: strangers choosing to guard a stranger's lie.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Tamsin POV. With hours left, the fleets maneuver for position, a saboteur aboard threatens the broadcast, and Sable realizes sustaining the lie means erasing the real last words of the Vessic dead. His crew fractures over whether mercy or truth matters more. Emotional beat: found family tested at the breaking point, love expressed as honest dissent.

chapters.title: What the Dead Actually Said
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At expiry, Sable broadcasts the true final message of Halcyon Reach — a lament, not a plea — translating it live in three tongues while the crew holds the transmitter under fire. The fleets, hearing grief instead of strategy, stand down; survivors emerge from the station's deep vaults. Emotional beat: belonging earned not by the lie he kept, but the truth he dared to speak.
